content.content:
trait Equality[\T extends Equality[\T\]\]
    opr =(self, other:T): Boolean = self SEQV other
end

(** Total ordering *)

object LexicographicPartialReduction
        extends { MonoidReduction[\Comparison\],
                  ReductionWithZeroes[\Comparison, Comparison\] }
    getter asString():String = "Lexicographic reduction on partial order"
    empty(): Comparison = EqualTo
    join(a:Comparison, b:Comparison):Comparison = a LEXICO b
    isZero(_:Unordered): Boolean = true
    isZero(_:Comparison): Boolean = false
end

object LexicographicReduction
        extends { MonoidReduction[\TotalComparison\],
                  ReductionWithZeroes[\TotalComparison, TotalComparison\] }
    getter asString():String = "Lexicographic reduction on total order"
    empty(): TotalComparison = EqualTo
    join(a:TotalComparison, b:TotalComparison):TotalComparison = a LEXICO b
    isLeftZero(_:EqualTo): Boolean = false
    isLeftZero(_:TotalComparison): Boolean = true
end

opr BIG LEXICO(): BigReduction[\TotalComparison, TotalComparison\] =
    BigReduction[\TotalComparison,TotalComparison\](LexicographicReduction)

opr BIG LEXICO(g: Generator[\TotalComparison\]) =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\TotalComparison,TotalComparison,TotalComparison,TotalComparison\](BIG LEXICO(), g)

trait Comparison
        extends { StandardPartialOrder[\Comparison\] }
        comprises { Unordered, TotalComparison }
    getter asString(): String
    opr =(self, other:Comparison): Boolean = false
    (** Lexicographic ordering.  First non-equal comparison dictates result. *)
    opr LEXICO(self, other:Comparison): Comparison = Unordered
    opr LEXICO(self, other:()->Comparison): Comparison = Unordered
    (** Symmetric comparison (total orders only).  All comparisons
        must be compatible, or Unordered results.  Compatible means
        "all the same sense or EqualTo" in which case the sense is the
        result (EqualTo if everything's EqualTo). *)
    opr SYMMETRIC_PARTIAL(self, other:Comparison): Comparison = Unordered
    opr SYMMETRIC_PARTIAL(self, other:()->Comparison): Comparison = self SYMMETRIC_PARTIAL other()
    opr INVERSE(self): Comparison
end

(** Unordered is the outcome of a CMP b when a and b are partially
    ordered and no ordering relationship exists between them. **)
object Unordered extends Comparison
    getter asString(): String = "Unordered"
    opr =(self, other:Unordered): Boolean = true
    opr <(self, other:Comparison): Boolean = false
    opr SYMMETRIC_PARTIAL(self, other:()->Comparison): Comparison = Unordered
    opr INVERSE(self): Comparison = Unordered
end

trait TotalComparison
        extends { Comparison, StandardMinMax[\TotalComparison\] }
        comprises { LessThan, EqualTo, GreaterThan }
    (* We're both a partial order (including Unordered) and a total
       order (TotalComparison alone).  Avoid ambiguity between the
       default definitions of CMP and >=. *)
    opr =(self, other:TotalComparison): Boolean = false
    opr =(self, other:Unordered): Boolean = false
    opr CMP(self, other:Unordered): Comparison = Unordered
    opr <(self, other:Unordered): Boolean = false
    opr >=(self, other:Unordered): Boolean = false
    opr >=(self, other:Comparison): Boolean = NOT (other < self)
    opr >=(self, other:TotalComparison): Boolean = NOT (self < other)
    opr <=(self, other:TotalComparison): Boolean = NOT (other < self)
    opr MIN(self, other:TotalComparison): TotalComparison = if other < self then other else self end
    opr MAX(self, other:TotalComparison): TotalComparison = if other < self then self else other end
    opr MINMAX(self, other:TotalComparison): (TotalComparison,TotalComparison) =
        if other < self then (other, self) else (self, other) end
    opr LEXICO(self, other:TotalComparison): TotalComparison = self
    opr LEXICO(self, other:()->TotalComparison): TotalComparison = self
    opr LEXICO(self, other:()->Comparison): Comparison = self
    opr INVERSE(self): TotalComparison
end

object LessThan extends TotalComparison
    getter asString(): String = "LessThan"
    opr =(self, other:LessThan): Boolean = true
    opr CMP(self, other:LessThan): TotalComparison = EqualTo
    opr CMP(self, other:TotalComparison): TotalComparison = GreaterThan
    opr <(self, other:LessThan): Boolean = false
    opr <(self, other:TotalComparison): Boolean = true
    opr SYMMETRIC_PARTIAL(self, other:LessThan): LessThan = LessThan
    opr SYMMETRIC_PARTIAL(self, other:EqualTo): LessThan = LessThan
    opr INVERSE(self): TotalComparison = GreaterThan
end

object GreaterThan extends TotalComparison
    getter asString(): String = "GreaterThan"
    opr =(self, other:GreaterThan): Boolean = true
    opr CMP(self, other:GreaterThan): TotalComparison = EqualTo
    opr CMP(self, other:TotalComparison): TotalComparison = LessThan
    opr <(self, other:TotalComparison): Boolean = false
    opr SYMMETRIC_PARTIAL(self, other:GreaterThan): GreaterThan = GreaterThan
    opr SYMMETRIC_PARTIAL(self, other:EqualTo): GreaterThan = GreaterThan
    opr INVERSE(self): TotalComparison = LessThan
end

object EqualTo extends TotalComparison
    getter asString(): String = "EqualTo"
    opr =(self, other:EqualTo): Boolean = true
    opr CMP(self, other:TotalComparison): TotalComparison = INVERSE other
    opr <(self, other:GreaterThan): Boolean = true
    opr <(self, other:TotalComparison): Boolean = false
    opr LEXICO(self, other:TotalComparison): TotalComparison = other
    opr LEXICO(self, other:()->TotalComparison): TotalComparison = other()
    opr LEXICO(self, other:()->Comparison): Comparison = other()
    opr SYMMETRIC_PARTIAL(self, other: Comparison): Comparison = other
    opr INVERSE(self): TotalComparison = EqualTo
end

content.content:
- F-70 **The compiled checker checks a static argument written at a dotted method call against its parameter's bound, but not one written at a top-level function call.** At a dotted call it puts the written arguments into each bound and refuses a call whose argument misses one, "No such method" (row 651, fixed). At a top-level call it matches kinds only, so `n[\String\]("d")` passes for `n[\T extends Number\](s: String): T` (row 470, open). Gated by `compiler_tests/MethodStaticArgsBoundNamesOther*`, which accept a dotted call whose written arguments meet their bounds. No test pins the refusal of an argument that misses its bound; a probe showed it (`rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 6). Row 470 can have no gated test, since the harness has no form for a program that the specification refuses and the checker accepts. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-250 **Inside a declaration, the compiled checker reads a `where` clause's trait constraint `X extends B` as a bound of `X`, and it adds a constraint on the declaration's own static parameter to that parameter's bound in the declaration's arrow (its function type), so a call is checked against it.** So a method's condition on its trait's or object's static parameter bounds that parameter in the method's body (`compiler_tests/WhereBoundMethodChecker`), and a call that breaks a function's own constraint is refused (`compiler_tests/XXXWhereBoundFunctionCall`, which refuses `g("s")`). A hole remains: a static argument written at a top-level call is not checked against that bound, so `g[\String\]("s")` is accepted (row 470). F-256 holds where the checker reads the constraints at a dotted call, at a type's use and at a `comprises` clause, with its other limits. The library edits that landed with this reading are F-242's (the generic `distribute`, and the `where` conditions on `SumReduction`'s `distribute` overloads for `MAX` and `MIN`) and F-85's (`additiveIdentity`'s and `multiplicativeIdentity`'s fallbacks written `cast[\T\](0)` and `cast[\T\](1)`, and `embiggen` typed `BigReduction[\T,T\]`). Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-library-distribute/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-256 **The compiled checker checks a `where` clause's trait constraints where they apply.** At a dotted call, a candidate whose `where` clause constrains its trait's or object's static parameter is not applicable where the receiver's static argument breaks the constraint ('Method Holder[\String\].showIt is not applicable: its where clause requires String to extend Shows.'). If a function's or method's `where` clause has a trait constraint, the clause's `nat` and `int` variables become static parameters of its arrow, inferred at the call. So a constraint whose bound names such a variable is met where some value of it meets every constraint. When the type variables' solutions leave only size constraints, the solver tries once more to solve them. Walk and the compiled path both refuse a function's or method's type `where`-clause variable at name binding ('E is undefined.'), so this inference never reaches one. A trait's or object's own constraint is checked where its type is used, with the bound's message, also at a constructor call through the call's type. A type `where`-clause variable of a `comprises` clause is bounded by its binding and by the clause's constraints on it, where it is opened and in the check of an extender. In a bound that names the variable itself, as `E extends StandardTotalOrder[\E\]` does, the opened type stands for the variable. Not read: at a dotted call, a constraint on the trait's or object's static parameter whose bound names the method's own static parameters or `where`-clause variables; at a type's use, a constraint whose bound names a `where`-clause variable; and a static argument written at a top-level call (row 470). Walk still runs a dotted call that breaks a method's condition (row 777), and a `comprises` clause's `where`-clause variable captures a same-named static parameter in another declaration's bound (row 778). These checks moved no site of the count or the distance (F-53 holds the current values). Tests: `compiler_tests/XXXWhereBoundDottedCallChecker`, `WhereVariableBoundCallChecker`, `XXXWhereConstraintTypeUseChecker`, `XXXWhereConstraintExtendsChecker`, `XXXComprisesWhereBoundExtenderChecker`, `OpenTypeWhereConstraintChecker`, `XXXComprisesWhereConstraintExtenderChecker`, `OpenTypeWhereSelfBoundChecker`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-checker-where-checks/REPORT.md`, sections 1 and 6, and `SKEPTIC.md` beside it.

- F-174 **The specification states the type group's 2011 overloading model: declarations of one name may differ in their static parameters, and a declaration with static parameters is read as one declaration over all its instances within its bounds.** It states P-45 and P-42. The section "Declarations with Static Parameters" states the OOPSLA 2011 paper's three rules: No Duplicates, Return Type and Meet. It gives one more restriction as the compiled path's, not the language's. Where one generic declaration is more specific than another with as many static parameters, the two must declare them of the same kinds, position by position. Also, the more specific one's return type must be a subtype of the other's when their static parameters are matched by position, so the checker refuses an override whose return type reorders its static parameters (row 398, fixed). The section "Principles of Overloading" forbids overloading a functional whose single parameter's type is a type parameter with the bound `Any` written, as `T extends Any`. A type parameter with no `extends` clause, whose bound is also `Any`, is exempt. Both paths refuse such an overload: the checker in `OverloadingChecker.checkBoundAny`, and walk since row 534's fix. Neither path runs every set that the rules allow. Appendix I's entry "Overloading with static parameters" names the sets that each path fails. In row 542, the checker refuses a generic declaration beside a plain one over an object type, as `ident[\T\](x: T): T` beside `ident(x: Circle): Circle`. In row 537, the code generator fails on two generic declarations whose bounds differ. In row 539, walk refuses at load the 2019 paper's valid set over an array list and a list. In rows 779 and 780, walk fails on two generic functional methods one of whose declared domains lies inside the other's: in a trait or object without static parameters it refuses them at load, and in a trait with static parameters it loads them, but a call to which both apply fails. case "$SETTING" in any|walk|compile) ;; *) echo "distance: unknown setting $SETTING" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac
FLAGS="-Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.all=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"
COMPONENTS="Library/FortressLibrary.fss Library/RangeInternals.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss Library/List.fss Library/String.fss Library/FlatString.fss Library/Stream.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fss Library/TypeProxy.fss Library/Writer.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss"

rm -rf "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" \
         "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')
if [ -z "$CP" ] ; then echo "distance: no classpath from bin/fortress_classpath" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
